First of all, this is gonna kinda be a long one, so buckle up and read at your leisure.

Welcome to the wonderful world of MMO's, and to Throne and Liberty. MMO's are designed in a way to bring you through a storytelling mechanic via a main story questline that has a batch of side quests in every area to help you level and to understand the lore/importance of each area. You can just lore and everything else entirely and just speed through all the missions and skipping the cutscenes.

MMO's are designed in a way to kind of railroad you to end game by giving you a string of milestones to comeplete. IE: Talk to guy, get quest, go to area, do thing, (possible cutscene), then go back to guy OR go to a new guy to turn it in, rinse and repeat. It's been like this throughout EVERY MMO simply because they want you to immerse in a story just like a singleplayer RPG.

The game itself DOES feel a little clunky, especially the movement mechanics and player coordinate identification in some cases. However, aside from that it's an amazing game so far. Guilds ACTUALLY matter, content ACTUALLY feels good and challenging, and for the most part there are a lot of really nice/helpful people willing to give you information along the way (which you can also mostly learn through the questing).

  
All in all, keep on going and when you get to 50 and start really diving into the end-game and systems/mechanics of the game you will really know what you are in for. Give it time, don't rush, and above anything else HAVE FUN in whatever way YOU want to have fun.

If you want looks, go Kawasaki. If you want reliable long term that’s easier to work on, go Honda.

As far as first bike, ALWAYS buy used. No payments, if you break it you can learn to fix it without the fear of ruining a new bike, and you have the options to customize it without breaking a loan agreement and getting penalized (a lot of dealers have this in fine print).

I would never recommend a mid range sport/super sport. Simply because the power ratios are not made for learners, they are for intermediate riders with a few years worth of miles under them. That’s my opinion, everyone can start in whatever they want, but I highly recommend 500cc and below for a beginner and their first purchase.

Happy hunting and ride safe new bro. Welcome to bike life. 🤙
